actions.reason: No change reached the 1% minimum on this tip. Measured: (1) a branching FieldElement::sub that adds the modulus only when the subtraction borrows: msm_ir 0.9999, decode_ir 0.9971, scalar_mul_ir 1.0000. The compiler already avoids most of that work. (2) Taking out the Jacobi pre-check in sqrt and instead checking root^2 == self: decode_ir 1.3304, much worse, because the decode inputs contain many non-residues and the binary Jacobi test is cheap. (3) Change (1) plus a shift-by-32 for the MODULUS[1] multiply-accumulate in the Montgomery reduction plus negation as p - y: decode_ir 0.9986, msm_ir 0.9993, scalar_mul_ir 1.0013, so the shift trick cancelled the gain. Outputs were identical every time. For msm_ir I estimated rather than measured some ideas: a wider point-side NAF, Pippenger for 32 points, and an add formula that trades a multiply for a square. By those estimates each costs about as much as it saves. Anything left at the group level probably needs a new formula, not small tweaks.

I tried three edits in secp256r1/src/field.rs. First, a branching FieldElement::sub that adds the modulus only when the subtraction borrows. Second, removing the Jacobi pre-check in sqrt and checking root^2 == self instead. Third, a later variant of the field.rs changes, 26 guarded lines in total.

The branching sub gave msm_ir 0.9999, decode_ir 0.9971, scalar_mul_ir 1.0000. It did not help, and the compiler already avoids most of that work. Dropping the Jacobi pre-check made decode_ir 1.3304, much worse. The third attempt gave decode_ir 0.9986, msm_ir 0.9993, scalar_mul_ir 1.0013. All three had identical outputs. All three were rejected against the required 0.9900. I submitted nothing.

On this tip, sub is already close to what the compiler can do. The Jacobi pre-check in sqrt pays for itself on the decode inputs, so keep it.

Next I will look at mul and montgomery_reduce in field.rs, and at the decode path itself, rather than sub or sqrt.
